_comment: Canonical project metadata. Single source of truth for the title and version. code/00_metadata.py renders CITATION.cff from this file; code/05_document.py sets the report title from it; code/build_pdf.sh reads the PDF title from it; code/03_qa.py fails the build if the README heading, the report, CITATION.cff or the rendered PDF disagree with it. title_ascii is the same title with the en-dash replaced by a hyphen, for contexts that cannot encode it (wkhtmltopdf's PDF document properties). Do not restate the title anywhere else.
title: Schema Evolution in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, 2021–2026: A Three-Source Reconstruction
title_ascii: Schema Evolution in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, 2021-2026: A Three-Source Reconstruction

release._comment: CANONICAL RELEASE STATE. One source of truth for draft/final mode, the DOI and the release date. code/release_state.py is the only reader; every generated artifact (README banner, CITATION.cff, the report's first page, the CISA issue text, the QA header, the figure stamps) derives from it. In draft mode doi and release_date are null and no DOI appears in any output. Setting mode to 'final' with either one unset or placeholder-shaped makes the build refuse to run.

author_verification._comment: Dates on which the author personally performed a verification step. These are historical facts about what a person did and must never be derived from a build date: docs/LIMITATIONS.md item 10 previously took this from stats.access_date, so re-running the pipeline on a later day silently changed the date on which the author was said to have checked the live CISA URLs. Caught during the final build for v0.1.0.
